newsitem.title: USA: FBI gets more than 1,000 bomb tips.
newsitem.headline: FBI gets more than 1,000 bomb tips.

text.p: Federal investigators said on Wednesday they have received hundreds of videotapes and photographs since appealing to the public for leads on the bombing of Centennial Olympic Park.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation has received "well over a thousand calls" to the toll-free hotline established on Monday for information on the July 27 bombing, spokesman Jay Spadafore said.
"We have several hundred good leads. Most of them involve video tapes and photographs," he said.

An Atlanta man said he gave the FBI a photograph of a white male who was carrying a backpack in the park about six hours before the bombing. Ted Miltiades said he reviewed his Olympic photos and found one of a man carrying a military-style backpack that appeared to be full.
FBI spokesman Spadafore would not comment on the photograph.
Calls to the toll-free telephone hotline, 1-888-324-9797, are answered at a phone bank in Washington, Spadafore said. Tips are then forwarded to the FBI's Atlanta office.
